html:
SMTO-AUT-0007 — This service sign-in isn't set up completely

GUID: 1cacb29a-6ba9-5f06-9f27-f137f6a1a308
Slug: auth-profile-invalid
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find a complete, up-to-date setup for this service sign-in, such as the app ID, its secret, or the sign-in address. Signing in again won't help until that setup is fixed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and find the sign-in connection SMTO named. Check that it exists and that the app entry it points to also exists. Each service sign-in has a connection entry and a separate app entry, and SMTO stops if either is missing.
  2. Ask the person who set up the app entry to check that its client ID, sign-in address, secret, and return address (redirect URI) are all filled in correctly. Without these, SMTO can't build a sign-in request the service will accept.
  3. If someone edited these entries while the Task was running, check whether the step already did anything, then ask SMTO to try it again. SMTO stops when an entry changes mid-task instead of mixing old and new settings.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the sign-in prompt, or the step continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't paste app secrets, passwords, or sign-in codes into the conversation or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The auth broker could not resolve a valid, current OAuth connection and client pair: a record is missing or wrongly keyed, fails profile validation, lacks required client settings (issuer or token endpoint, secret, key or redirect URI), or changed revision mid-operation.

What this means

  • OAuth setup cannot resolve a valid current connection/client profile, required endpoint, or referenced profile revision. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth setup cannot resolve a valid current connection/client profile, required endpoint, or referenced profile revision.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the saved connection, client reference, required endpoints and current parameter revisions.

How to fix it

  • In Parameter Store, confirm the oauth2_connection key exists (lower-case canonical key), its client_ref names a valid oauth2_client, and the client passes auth/profiles.validate: issuer or token_endpoint, a client_auth_method with its secret, key or certificate, a redirect_uri ending in /api/agent/auth/oauth/callback for browser grants, and HTTPS endpoints. If a referenced record changed during the operation, check whether the earlier operation had any effect before starting a new authorization.
  • Select the intended saved OAuth connection and repair its referenced client configuration or stale parameter revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected connection resolves a valid current client profile with the endpoints its grant requires.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
